samples.claim: SparseValiditySet has Meaning meaning=1 and SparsePositionSet positions=2. Meaning UNSPECIFIED=0, NULL_POSITIONS=1 (stored positions null, all others valid), VALID_POSITIONS=2 (inverse). Empty and All position markers are separate empty messages. samples.claim: Public field_id has a TODO to reduce visibility but currently returns a Schema error with fixed Vector column not in schema text on any failed path lookup. top_level_field_ids returns root IDs in order; field_ids collects pre-order IDs, including negatives. field_by_id_mut and field_by_id check each root itself then its descendants, so unlike the Field versions they include top-level nodes. First forward DFS match wins if IDs are duplicated.
samples.review_note: Matches public TODO, fixed Schema error text, root inclusion and field_ids iteration. Additionally inspected Field descendant-only search at1113-1139 and Schema pre-order stack at82-112.

samples.claim: validate first rejects dots and duplicates among top-level names. It collects reserved negative lineage IDs only from top-level fields whose name maps to that same ID, then pre-order checks every ID: negative IDs outside that allowed set fail, and every duplicate fails. A nested reuse of an allowed reserved ID eventually fails duplication against its top-level owner. It does not check lineage datatype/nullability, parent_id consistency or nested name uniqueness. Every field's reconstructed DataType is passed to fixed-size-list dimension validation; malformed Field::data_type may panic before returning a validation error. Primary-key verification is a separate call, not part of validate.
samples.review_note: Matches top-level names/reserved IDs/duplicate checks and dimension call. Additionally inspected Field::data_type at171-193 for panic paths; primary-key validation remains separate.

samples.claim: test_backoff_with_base sets base three/no jitter and expects 50,150,450ms. test_backoff_with_unit sets 100/no jitter and expects 100,200ms. Other settings retain defaults.
samples.review_note: Matches both backoff test builders and every asserted millisecond value.

samples.claim: UpdateMapEntry has key string=1 and optional value string=2: absent value removes the key, while present empty string stores an empty value. UpdateMap.update_entries repeated=1 applies changes and replace bool=2 selects full replacement versus merge. Duplicate-key ordering and deletion during replacement require converter evidence.
samples.review_note: Matches optional value and replace contract; present empty differs from absence. Converter ordering remains explicitly pending.

samples.claim: CompactRemapStep::get extracts high32 fragment and low32 offset. Missing fragment returns outer None; an offset >= supplied physical rows also returns None. Missing retained offset inside a covered fragment returns Some(None). A present offset produces preceding-retained-count + zero-based rank, uses group_idx to locate its destination layout, and returns Some(Some(new address)). Without physical counts, every absent offset in a listed fragment is treated as deleted.
samples.review_note: Matches every get branch, physical bound and nested Option result exactly.

HashSet formula/default are at rust/lance-core/src/deepsize.rs:38-44 and rust/lance-core/src/deepsize.rs:213-220.

samples.claim: merge converts Other and resets its IDs. It clones each Self root, merges a matching Other field with Field::merge, then appends new Other roots in Other order, suppressing repeated root names already in the output. Metadata begins with Other then Self overwrites shared keys. It returns a new Schema without assigning new IDs or validating it; imported fields stay -1 until explicit set_field_id, as tested below. Self is unmodified if conversion/merge fails; partial mutations affect only local clones.
samples.review_note: Matches clone/merge/append/metadata order and lack of ID assignment. Additionally read reset_id and test_merge_schemas_and_assign_field_ids at2371-2413 for imported -1 and explicit reassignment.

samples.claim: Private SchemaFieldIterPreOrder stores a Vec<&Field> stack. new reserves twice top-level count and pushes top-level fields in reverse. Iterator::next pops a field, pushes its children reversed and yields the parent; thus traversal preserves source order in depth-first pre-order. Exhaustion returns None; no recursive call stack is used, but pending siblings consume heap stack space.
samples.review_note: Matches stack allocation, reversed pushes and forward pre-order traversal; no recursive iterator call.

samples.claim: pad_bytes<const ALIGN:usize>(n:usize)->usize debug-asserts is_pwr_two(ALIGN as u64), then computes (ALIGN-(n&(ALIGN-1)))&(ALIGN-1). For a valid nonzero power-of-two alignment it gives zero for aligned n, otherwise bytes to next boundary, without first adding ALIGN to n. Doctest ALIGN=8 checks n=0/1/8/9 gives 0/7/0/7. Invalid alignment is not validated with a returned error and debug_assert may be disabled.
samples.review_note: Matches debug assertion, bit formula and all four doctest examples; invalid alignment is not a Result path.

samples.claim: FieldCoverage.offset_bitmaps=1 is a repeated bytes list with one 32-bit Roaring bitmap per data_file.fields entry in the same order. A present offset whose value is NULL overrides to NULL; an absent offset falls through to base. A sparse NULL update must not be encoded by simply omitting the offset.

245 |    * means the cell is overridden to NULL (distinct from an offset that is absent,
246 |    * which falls through to the base data file).
247 |    */
248 |   repeated bytes offset_bitmaps = 1;
249 | }
250 |
samples.review_note: Matches per-field bitmap order and distinction between covered NULL and absent offset.

samples.claim: verify_primary_key gathers marked fields, rejects any non-leaf, then walks actual ancestry (if found) including the field itself and rejects nullable members, List/LargeList logical types and Map logical types. It does not explicitly reject FixedSizeList, whose primitive-element representation can be a leaf; it does not verify positions, duplicate positions, value uniqueness or clustering-key constraints. Publicly malformed schemas with duplicate IDs can confuse ancestry; missing ancestry simply skips that loop. No data values are read, consistent with unenforced key naming.
samples.review_note: Matches non-leaf/nullable/List/LargeList/Map checks. Additionally inspected ancestry634-648 and is_leaf1166-1168; primitive fixed-size-list representation is covered in the reviewed Arrow conversion.

samples.claim: BTreeMap estimates len*(size_of::<K>()+size_of::<V>()+3*size_of::<usize>()) plus live key/value children. BTreeSet uses len*(size_of::<K>()+3*size_of::<usize>()) plus live key children. Comments motivate roughly three pointer words per entry based on an average B-tree node. These formulas do not inspect actual node count, node occupancy or allocations.
samples.review_note: Matches both B-tree formulas and approximate three-pointer rationale, with allocator/occupancy limitations retained.

samples.claim: OrderedCompactionMapping derives Debug and privately owns Arc<RowAddrRemap>. Documentation calls it an adapter for one group's existing bitmap/rank remap, explicitly not replacing the legacy FRI reader or writer. Public new simply stores the Arc; its documentation presumes fragment layout validation happened when the remap was constructed, and no additional validation is performed here.
samples.review_note: Matches adapter scope, private Arc state and constructor validation precondition without a validator call.

samples.claim: exclude accepts a Debug TryInto<Self>; conversion failures are replaced with a generic Schema error, losing the original reason. All roots are looked up by parsed paths, not literal unescaped names.
